solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Rewrite score/poem (9)

blocks.note: read on the surface as an editor's order to redo some text
the slash offers two things one might write afresh: music or verse; the answer is the verb for writing either one again

annotation.surface: A terse instruction to an artist to redo a piece of work.
annotation.walkthrough: RECOMPOSE covers both: to compose is to write a score or a poem, and doing it again is to recompose.
annotation.definitionFit: To recompose is literally to compose again, whether the work is music or verse.

entries.clue: Censure theatre with nothing brought in for mounting (7)

indicatorNotes.brought in: O is carried inside the next piece
indicatorNotes.mounting: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: nothing = O, zero; it goes inside ROF to make ROOF

annotation.surface: Critics condemning a theatre for staging a play with nothing new in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a mere connector, but it is the letters that get turned upwards and then filled with O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: censure and reproof are both formal words for an expression of disapproval.

entries.clue: Thinking party making each side right (11)

indicatorNotes.making each side right: each L (left) in the party word becomes R (right)

annotation.surface: A political party that pushes every faction to the right wing, dressed up as a think tank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Side' is the key: left and right are the two sides, abbreviated L and R, so turning the left side right swaps the letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Cerebration is the act of thinking, from cerebrum, the brain.

entries.clue: Extract money from millions using low council tax just introduced (5)

indicatorNotes.just introduced: only the introductions, the opening letters, of those words are used

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

annotation.surface: A complaint about a government squeezing millions of people through a new council tax.
annotation.walkthrough: Council tax is the British local property tax, which makes the surface sound like a real news item about fleecing households.
annotation.definitionFit: To mulct is to fine or swindle someone, taking money from them.

entries.clue: What shingles will do above the tops of one’s legs? (7)

blocks.note: your lap is the top of your thighs when seated

annotation.surface: A question about where the painful rash shingles tends to spread on the body.
annotation.walkthrough: Shingles suggests the illness; here they are the overlapping wooden roof tiles.
annotation.definitionFit: Roof shingles are laid so each one overlaps the one below it.

entries.clue: Green energy company (3)

annotation.surface: A green energy company, the sort that sells renewable electricity.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one noun phrase; the definition is only its first word.
annotation.definitionFit: Eco- as a prefix or informal adjective means environmentally friendly, green.

entries.clue: Confusion with em dash and good English? (7)

blocks.note: em spelled out is the letter M

annotation.surface: A typesetter's muddle over when to use an em dash in good English.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Em dash' is a genuine punctuation mark, so the eye reads it as one item; split it, and em is M while dash is spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: A mélange is a mixture, a jumble, so a confusion of things.

entries.clue: Creature God completed with miracle regularly (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at even steps: every second one

blocks.note: Mars, the Roman god of war

annotation.surface: A creation story: God finished making a creature by a miracle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward Genesis; the capital G hides that the god is a specific one, Mars.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the pouched mammals such as kangaroos belong to the wider class of creatures.

entries.clue: Down the back of gloomy topless drinking establishment (6)

indicatorNotes.topless: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so it goes

annotation.surface: A grim topless bar, with its seedy associations.
annotation.walkthrough: Topless suggests the kind of bar; it is the instruction to behead GLUM.
annotation.definitionFit: Lumbar describes the lower part of the back, so a pain there is down the back.

entries.clue: Reported securing arch-villain breaking line in well-policed event (7,4,8)

indicatorNotes.Reported: the answer is spelt like a word that sounds like 'knotting'
indicatorNotes.breaking: the villain's letters are broken up and rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: the L joins the letters being rearranged

blocks.note: knotting = securing, said the same as NOTTING
L = line; added in before the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A news report of a master criminal caught crossing a police line at a heavily policed event.
annotation.walkthrough: The Notting Hill Carnival is London's huge annual Caribbean street festival, known for its large police presence.
annotation.definitionFit: The carnival draws a million people each August and thousands of police officers.

entries.clue: Fine constraining rodent’s wandering (7)

indicatorNotes.constraining: the fine holds the rodent inside it

blocks.note: an eric was a blood fine in old Irish law
a rat; it sits inside ER…IC

annotation.surface: A fine tying down a rodent that keeps roaming about.
annotation.walkthrough: ERIC as a fine is an old word that crosswords keep alive; the reader sees a name and must think of a penalty.
annotation.definitionFit: Erratic, from Latin errare, originally meant wandering, and still describes a straying course.

entries.clue: Place with fighting men in space base? (5)

blocks.note: an em is a printer's unit of space
a bed is a base, as a road bed

annotation.surface: A military posting, perhaps soldiers stationed at a base in space.
annotation.walkthrough: An embed is a war correspondent placed with a fighting unit; to embed a reporter is exactly this.
annotation.definitionFit: To embed a journalist is to place them with troops in the field.

entries.clue: The author’s collected by car after leaving last bar (9)

indicatorNotes.collected by: the car picks up the other piece inside it
indicatorNotes.after leaving last: the car loses its final letter

blocks.note: ESTATE (an estate car, a station wagon) without its last letter
the author's = mine, the setter's; it goes inside ESTA…T

annotation.surface: A writer is given a lift home after last orders at the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinking scene, and bar is indeed the definition: an estaminet is a small French café-bar.
annotation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small bar or café in France or Belgium.

entries.clue: British and India afterwards join forces — and how it’s arranged? (11)

blocks.note: India is I in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: Britain and India forming an alliance, and a question about the terms of the deal.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole scene: two countries uniting is an arrangement made bilaterally, between two sides.
annotation.definitionFit: An arrangement between two nations is made bilaterally.

entries.clue: Get right into doing up one’s home that’s in need of cleaning (5)

indicatorNotes.Get: together with 'into', an instruction to put one piece inside another
indicatorNotes.into: 'into' marks motion inwards, so RT is moved inside DIY

blocks.note: DIY = do-it-yourself home improvement; RT goes inside it

annotation.surface: Advice to throw yourself into renovating a home that needs a good clean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get right into' reads as 'commit fully to'; split up, it tells you to put RT inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: whatever is soiled, dirty, calls for cleaning.

entries.clue: Plane shape seating everyone between Margo and Pearl when flying (13)

indicatorNotes.seating: ALL is given a seat among the other letters
indicatorNotes.between: ALL goes in among the two names
indicatorNotes.when flying: the names' letters fly about and land in a new order

blocks.note: all = everyone; seated among the other letters

annotation.surface: An airline seating plan: everyone placed between two passengers called Margo and Pearl on a flight.
annotation.walkthrough: Plane suggests an aircraft, which the seating and flying keep up; in geometry a plane shape is a flat figure.
annotation.definitionFit: A parallelogram is a flat four-sided figure with two pairs of parallel sides.

entries.clue: Extremely thievish scoundrel grabbing large choker (9)

indicatorNotes.Extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: L = large; it goes inside ROTT…ER

annotation.surface: A thieving villain snatching a big necklace.
annotation.walkthrough: A choker in the surface is jewellery; the answer takes it as someone who chokes people.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal agent noun: one who throttles squeezes the throat, which is what choking someone means.

entries.clue: Vocal about what can restrain route circling city (7)

indicatorNotes.about: ORAL goes around the other piece

blocks.note: a horse's bit restrains it; it sits inside OR…AL

annotation.surface: Protesters speaking out about restrictions on a ring road.
annotation.walkthrough: An orbital is a ring road around a city; the M25 around London is often called the London Orbital.
annotation.definitionFit: An orbital road circles a city, like an orbit.

entries.clue: Strong wave I felt round orbiting star (7)

indicatorNotes.round: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so I and MAT are read backwards
indicatorNotes.orbiting: the turned letters circle the star

blocks.note: felt can be matted into a mat; IMAT reads backwards as TAMI
the sun is a star; it goes inside T…AMI

annotation.surface: Someone describing a powerful wave of feeling for a celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Felt' and 'star' read as emotion and celebrity; as nouns they are a mat and the sun.
annotation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge, destructive sea wave.

entries.clue: Book of Hobbes, say — the thing that kept Churchill going? (6,3,4,6)

blocks.note: Thomas Hobbes, the philosopher, is one Thomas

blocks.clueFragment: the thing that kept Churchill going
blocks.note: the Churchill was a British Second World War tank, powered by its engine

annotation.surface: A literary puzzle: which work of Hobbes sustained Churchill through the war?
annotation.walkthrough: The surface invites Leviathan and wartime fortitude. The Churchill is the tank named after him, and Thomas the Tank Engine is the children's railway book series.
annotation.definitionFit: Thomas the Tank Engine is the hero and title of the Rev. W. Awdry's children's books.

entries.clue: Note insect by tip of canary grass (7)

indicatorNotes.tip of: the tip here is the end, so the last letter

blocks.note: ti, a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher's note of an insect beside a canary.
annotation.walkthrough: Canary grass is a real plant, so 'canary grass' looks like the definition; only 'grass' is, and timothy is a different grass.
annotation.definitionFit: Timothy is a meadow grass grown for hay.

entries.clue: Fear of dictator not liking his neighbours (12)

blocks.note: a phobia is a fear of something

annotation.surface: A dictator who is afraid, and who dislikes the people next door.
annotation.walkthrough: Fear of Franco is Franco-phobia, and Franco's neighbours across the Pyrenees were the French, whom a francophobe dislikes.
annotation.definitionFit: Francophobia is dislike of France, Spain's neighbour, so of Franco's neighbours.

entries.clue: One going to face dog beginning to rampage (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the first letter of the next word

annotation.surface: Someone about to confront a dog that is starting to run wild.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Face' sounds like confrontation; it is the coalface, where a collier, a coal miner, works.
annotation.definitionFit: A collier goes down the mine to work at the coalface.

entries.clue: Selfish move for one Conservative in case (10)

indicatorNotes.for: 'for' in the sense of 'in exchange for': GO is put in place of a C
indicatorNotes.in: the swap happens inside the word for case

blocks.note: a case is an oddball, an eccentric
a go is a move in a game
C = Conservative; one of ECCENTRIC's two Cs is replaced by GO

annotation.surface: A Tory accused of a self-serving political move over some affair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a legal case; it means an odd person, as in 'he's a real case'.
annotation.definitionFit: An egocentric person thinks only of themselves, so is selfish.

entries.clue: Confront orchestra no good in constant echo (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the orchestra and NG go inside C…E

blocks.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
Echo is E in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: A conductor taking on a poor orchestra that keeps producing echoes.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hallé is a famous orchestra based in Manchester, England; the accent drops in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to face up to someone and dispute with them.

entries.clue: Carole upset Sibyl perhaps (6)

indicatorNotes.upset: the name's letters are knocked over into a new order

annotation.surface: Carole has upset her friend Sibyl.
annotation.walkthrough: Both names look like people; Sibyl is really a sibyl, a prophetess of the ancient world.
annotation.definitionFit: A sibyl was a prophetess, an oracle; 'perhaps' marks her as one example.

entries.clue: Vessel from China bearing greetings (5)

indicatorNotes.bearing: the friend carries the greeting inside

blocks.note: china = mate, from rhyming slang china plate
hi = a greeting; it goes inside P…AL

annotation.surface: A ship arriving from China with messages of goodwill.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C sells the country; china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate. The vessel is a small bottle, not a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, a vessel for liquids.

entries.clue: Insistence discharge housing gives out light (9)

indicatorNotes.housing: PUS houses the next piece inside it

blocks.note: pus, a discharge from a wound

annotation.surface: A notice insisting that an electrical discharge from housing is giving off light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' sounds electrical; it is the medical kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Pushiness is forceful insistence on getting your way.

entries.clue: King endlessly shown right round one city in Belgium (9)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: the king loses his last letter

annotation.surface: A king being shown around a Belgian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Round' reads as a preposition, as in shown round; it is the letter O. ROI is also French for king, a nice touch in a Belgian name.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the clue gives the kind of place, a Belgian city, rather than a synonym.

entries.clue: Revolutionary notes key shift (7)

blocks.note: mi is a note of the sol-fa scale; plural mis

annotation.surface: A revolutionary's writings mark a crucial change of direction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key shift' reads as a major change; the definition is shift alone, a loose dress.
annotation.definitionFit: A chemise is a simple loose dress or undergarment, also called a shift.

entries.clue: Bone from rabbit’s tail found in Spanish dish (7)

indicatorNotes.tail: the tail is the last letter
indicatorNotes.found in: that letter goes inside the dish

blocks.note: the last letter of rabbiT; it goes inside PA…ELLA

annotation.surface: A diner finds a bone from a rabbit in their paella.
annotation.walkthrough: Rabbit is a genuine paella ingredient, so the surface is a plausible complaint to a waiter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the kneecap is one particular bone.

entries.clue: Poker is about deceits (7)

annotation.surface: Poker is a game built on deception.
annotation.walkthrough: Porkies are lies, from rhyming slang pork pies; fitting for a game of bluffing.
annotation.definitionFit: Porkies (pork pies) is British slang for lies, so deceits.

entries.clue: Far from dispassionate distribution of entailments (11)

indicatorNotes.distribution of: the letters are shared out in a new order

annotation.surface: An emotional quarrel over how a family estate is divided among heirs.
annotation.walkthrough: An entailment settles who inherits a property, so 'distribution' sounds like a will being read.
annotation.definitionFit: Sentimental means swayed by feeling, the opposite of dispassionate.

entries.clue: US city supported by the Republican state (6)

indicatorNotes.supported by: in a down clue, the city sits on top of what follows

annotation.surface: An American city propped up by the Republican state government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' is not a US state; it is a state of agitation, as in getting in a lather.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'in a lather' means agitated, in a state, from the foam on a sweating horse.

entries.clue: Remodelled porch left with holly, green in leaf and branch (11)

indicatorNotes.Remodelled: the letters are rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A porch rebuilt and decked with holly, green in leaf and branch, like a Christmas doorway.
annotation.walkthrough: The holly belongs to the surface decoration and to the fodder at once; the definition is the whole green-leaf phrase at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in leaves and stems.

entries.clue: Imagined one was at the opera for a musical? (7)

annotation.definition2: one was at the opera for a musical

blocks.note: an adjective: unreal, existing only in the mind, as a ghost seems to

blocks.clueFragment: one was at the opera for a musical
blocks.note: a description of a Lloyd Webber musical's title: the ghostly figure haunting the Paris Opera

annotation.surface: Someone wondering whether they only dreamt of attending a musical at the opera house.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition describes The Phantom of the Opera rather than naming it: a phantom was at the opera.
annotation.definitionFit: A phantom pain or threat is imagined, not real.

entries.clue: Fresh material on origins of intergalactic matter (11)

indicatorNotes.origins of: take the first letters of the next words

blocks.note: the first letters of intergalactic and matter
material = relevant, pertinent; 'on' places it after IM

annotation.surface: New research on where intergalactic matter comes from.
annotation.walkthrough: Fresh and material look scientific (new, substance); they mean cheeky and relevant.
annotation.definitionFit: Fresh, of a person, means cheeky or impertinent.

entries.clue: Rep cut scene in play for rotten character (11)

indicatorNotes.in play: the letters are loose, free to move

annotation.surface: A repertory company cutting a scene from a play because of a disreputable character.
annotation.walkthrough: The theatre words all sell the stage; 'in play' is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Putrescence is the state of rotting, a rotten character or quality.

entries.clue: Noticed aria needs rewriting or complete removal (11)

indicatorNotes.needs rewriting: the letters must be written out again in another order

annotation.surface: A critic spots that an aria must be rewritten or cut entirely.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an opera producer's note; 'or' simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Eradication means rooting out, removing completely.

entries.clue: In sharp pain I came down with unknown weakness (11)

blocks.note: lit = alighted, came down, as a bird does

annotation.surface: A patient describing falling ill with a mysterious weakness and a sharp pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Came down with' reads as catching an illness; split, it is LIT (landed) and the unknown Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lack of steadiness is a weakness in a structure or a person.

entries.clue: Following leaderless army corp is beyond what is reasonable (7)

indicatorNotes.leaderless: the word for following loses its first letter

blocks.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

annotation.surface: Criticism that an army corps' conduct has gone too far after losing its commander.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless army' looks like one idea; the leaderless word is 'Following', and the army corps is REME.
annotation.definitionFit: Extreme means going beyond what is reasonable or moderate.

entries.clue: Charge pounds in international shows? I have (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed within, so L sits inside the shows

blocks.note: L = pounds (librae); it goes inside EXP…OS

annotation.surface: An exhibitor asking about the cost in pounds at international shows, and answering yes.
annotation.walkthrough: Charge sounds like a fee, and pounds like money; the charge is the kind that blows up.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised sense: a charge in mining or demolition is the quantity of explosive set to go off.

entries.clue: A number’s outside set down range (9)

indicatorNotes.outside: A and NINES sit outside PEN

blocks.note: to pen is to write, set down
nine's, the number with its s

annotation.surface: A number placed outside a set range of values.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' sounds mathematical beside 'number' and 'set'; it is a mountain range in Italy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Apennines are the mountain range running down Italy.

entries.clue: Relation arrived in state (9)

blocks.note: arr. = arrived, as on a timetable; it goes inside N…ATION

annotation.surface: A family member has turned up in the state.
annotation.walkthrough: Relation reads as a relative; it is the act of relating a story.
annotation.definitionFit: Relation in the sense of telling a story is narration.

entries.clue: Tons like note’s good style (5)

blocks.note: te, a note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Praise for a musical note's sense of style.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is' and joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone with taste has a sense of good style.

entries.clue: Prize view of person working on chimney? (10)

blocks.note: a chimney sweep, with the possessive s
someone's take on something is their view of it

annotation.surface: A chimney sweep's opinion on who should win an award.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads SWEEP'S TAKE, the sweep's view.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweepstake is a lottery whose pooled stakes go to the winner as a prize.

entries.clue: What’s also on course for Derby? A group from Sherwood? (3,4)

annotation.definition: What’s also on course for Derby?

blocks.clueFragment: What’s also on course for Derby?
blocks.note: a question about a classic flat race run at Epsom, the same course as the Derby
Sherwood Forest is famous for its oaks

annotation.surface: Horse racing and Robin Hood, with Derby and Sherwood both hinting at England's Midlands.
annotation.walkthrough: Derby and Sherwood Forest are both near Nottingham, which draws the eye to geography. The Derby and the Oaks are both flat races run at Epsom, England.
annotation.definitionFit: The Oaks is a race on the Derby's course; oaks are Sherwood's trees.

entries.clue: Soldier signals for a supply of bread? (7,5)

annotation.surface: A soldier signalling for bread to be supplied to the troops.
annotation.walkthrough: Bread is slang for money, so a supply of bread is an income.
annotation.definitionFit: Private means are an income from investments or inheritance, a supply of money.

entries.clue: What was performed on The Globe circle? (7)

annotation.surface: A question about what plays were staged at Shakespeare's Globe theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: The Globe was Shakespeare's theatre; 'performed on' suggests a stage, but the answer is an instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A theorbo is a large bass lute of the 17th century, played in performance.

entries.clue: Woodland god at the beginning can exist still (7)

indicatorNotes.at the beginning: take the first letters of the next two words

blocks.note: a silen is a woodland god, after Silenus
first letters of can and exist

annotation.surface: A woodland god can remain unchanged since the start of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as an adverb, 'yet'; it is the noun or verb meaning quiet.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: 'still' as in 'the still of the night' means quietness.

entries.clue: Prompt support for jockey losing first of races (4,2)

indicatorNotes.losing: to lose something is to be left without it, so the jockey's support is left without a letter
indicatorNotes.first of: the dropped letter is the first of races

blocks.note: a stirrup supports a rider's foot
one R (the first letter of races) is removed

annotation.surface: A jockey's gear failing and costing them the first race.
annotation.walkthrough: Prompt looks like an adjective meaning punctual; it is a verb, to provoke.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: to prompt a reaction is to provoke or agitate it.

entries.clue: Depression is concerning during revolution (7)

blocks.note: on = about, concerning; it goes inside CYCL…E

annotation.surface: A worry about the gloom that accompanies political revolution.
annotation.walkthrough: Depression is the weather kind, a low-pressure system.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a system of low pressure, a meteorological depression.

entries.clue: Cheat about 12 out of 500 (5)

indicatorNotes.out of: D (500) is taken out of the dozen

blocks.note: DOZEN without D, the Roman numeral for 500

annotation.surface: A swindler taking about 12 from a sum of 500.
annotation.walkthrough: '12 out of 500' reads as a ratio; it means 12 (DOZEN) with 500 (D) taken out.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned synonym: cozen survives mainly in literature and crosswords, meaning to cheat by trickery.

entries.clue: Bag shot game (7)

blocks.note: to bag is to net, catch
shot, as in cannon shot, is a ball

annotation.surface: A shooter bagging game birds.
annotation.walkthrough: Bag, shot and game all read as hunting; game is the definition, a sport.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: netball is one particular team game.

entries.clue: Book Zwickau’s leader into east European city in Germany (7)

indicatorNotes.into: 'into' marks motion inwards, so Z goes inside the two Es

blocks.note: first letter of Zwickau; it goes between the two Es
Kiel, a port in northern Germany

annotation.surface: Booking a trip from Zwickau to an eastern European city in Germany.
annotation.walkthrough: Book reads as a verb, to reserve; it is a book of the Bible.
annotation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is a prophetic book of the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Books exist to be taken up as a source of inspiration (5)

indicatorNotes.to be taken up: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a collection of books
are = exist; OT and ARE together are then read upwards

annotation.surface: Books are there to be picked up and inspire the reader.
annotation.walkthrough: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, patron of love poetry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: each of the nine Muses was a source of inspiration, and she is the Muse of love poetry.

entries.clue: A new unknown island by port in Italy led by unknown islander (9)

blocks.note: z, an algebraic unknown; the second 'unknown' in the clue, placed first
Bari, a port on Italy's Adriatic coast

annotation.surface: A newly found island near an Italian port, first seen by a mysterious islander.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue lists A-N-Z-I-BARI, then says the whole is led by one more unknown, which goes at the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A Zanzibari is a native of Zanzibar, an island off East Africa.

entries.clue: Renovated an incinerator swapping over bodies (13)

indicatorNotes.Renovated: the letters are rebuilt in a new order

annotation.surface: A refurbished incinerator where bodies are changed over, a dark crematorium scene.
annotation.walkthrough: The crematorium picture of bodies and an incinerator makes the answer, a soul moving to a new body, darkly apt.
annotation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is the soul passing from one body into another.

entries.clue: Cold work for one on the beat? (3)

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap

annotation.surface: A chilly job for a drummer keeping time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the beat' suggests music; it is a police officer's patrol route.
annotation.definitionFit: A cop walks the beat, the area they patrol.

entries.clue: Relative that is buried in northern church (5)

indicatorNotes.buried in: IE goes inside the other letters

annotation.surface: A family member laid to rest in a church in the north.
annotation.walkthrough: The funeral picture is apt; the buried thing is the abbreviation i.e.
annotation.definitionFit: A niece is a relative, your sibling's daughter.

entries.clue: Become increasingly inclined to go over protected by gun (7)

indicatorNotes.over: the word for go is turned over
indicatorNotes.protected by: something protected by a guard is surrounded by it, so the gun's letters go around EEP

blocks.note: the Sten gun, a British submachine gun
to pee (to go, to the toilet) turned over; it sits inside ST…EN

annotation.surface: Someone more and more tempted to go over to the enemy under armed guard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' suggests being willing; it is literal slope. 'Go' is the euphemism for urinating.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal sense: a slope that steepens becomes more inclined, more nearly vertical.

entries.clue: Not entirely sleepy tot or pupil around first form (9)

indicatorNotes.Not entirely: the answer uses only part of these words
indicatorNotes.around: read the letters the other way round

annotation.surface: A sleepy toddler or schoolchild half-awake at the start of the first class.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First form' reads as a school's first year, matching tot and pupil; it is an original model.
annotation.definitionFit: A prototype is the first form of something, from which later versions are made.
